milestones.description:
Goal: one traceable release image with full product acceptance and a viable maintenance path.

Complete when:
- The complete binding functional, visual, security, privacy, recovery and endurance test matrix demonstrably passes on the delivered image.
- Installation, upgrades and independent recovery work on supported hardware with controlled preservation/erasure options.
- The predefined stability, performance, memory, energy and data-integrity budgets are met on the required profile.
- Independent reproduction, Dutch user documentation, SBOM/licences, a patch policy, a reporting channel and support are in place.
- All required new and previously accepted criteria have been checked on the combined release within their evidence boundaries.

Integrates all product workstreams. The former 20→50% issue #43 is a historical work route, not a separate release score. Physical execution, signing and public release each require their own specific, separate authorisation.
Source: [Full test release](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/FULL-TEST-RELEASE.md).

milestones.description:
Goal: complete boot, distribution, privacy and security-boundary work in a verifiable way.

Complete when:
- Image/boot verification, key rotation, dependencies and build provenance for the release profile have been defined and independently checked.
- All applicable native privacy tests pass, including permission combinations, separate app/download permissions, network-free AI and the absence of telemetry or silent fallback.
- External experts have examined the agreed kernel, service, DMA, parser and capability boundaries; blocking findings have been resolved.
- The selected machine-checked invariants and remaining risks have been documented with their evidence boundaries.

Security is developed throughout all milestones; this is the combined final review. B03 has already been accepted; #41 retains additional production/key-rotation work. #248 concerns publication preparation and does not authorise a change to repository visibility.
Sources: [Rubric](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/progress.json) and [Privacy contract](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/LOCAL-PRIVACY-CONTRACT.md).

milestones.description:
Goal: run demonstrably useful system AI entirely on the user's own device.

Complete when:
- An actual local model performs the agreed core tasks on new input within the defined quality, memory and response budgets.
- Only selected context is available through the permitted broker route; cancellation and resource limits work.
- Model management/download is separate from personal context and inference; inference and helpers are given no network route.
- A missing model, offline use and insufficient resources are handled understandably without cloud or NAS inference.

milestones.description:
Goal: personal or shared NAS storage and multiple devices with understandable end-to-end protection.

Complete when:
- The client and NAS connect on the project's own OS using verified identities; content, names and sensitive metadata remain unreadable to the NAS administrator.
- Offline work, automatic resumption, conflicts, concurrent writers and network transitions do not cause silent data loss.
- Adding/revoking devices, key rotation, recovery, quotas and revocation by the NAS administrator work natively; old sessions do not revive.
- The existing external-provider function stores only client-side encrypted opaque objects, without content keys, escrow or silent fallback (FR-P06).

Hard dependencies: B02 plus native networking, TLS and network permissions. Host NAS/TLS trials are preparatory evidence.
Sources: [NAS contract](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/implementation/NAS-SHARING-AND-INTERNET.md) and [Object encryption](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/implementation/ENCRYPTED-OBJECT-STORAGE.md).

Acceptance: docs/progress.json remains the source for weighted progress. Closure requires source-linked evidence at the prescribed level; a host test, merge or static Graphify analysis does not replace native/product acceptance. No calendar deadline has been set.

milestones.description:
Goal: usable native internet with authenticated connections and enforceable permissions per app and destination.

Complete when:
- Address configuration, DNS, routes, disconnection/resumption and permitted internet connections work.
- Maintained TLS/cryptography with the selected hybrid PQC route works natively; incorrect peers and negative handshakes are rejected without silent insecure fallback.
- Permissions, revocation of live connections and helper routes are enforced natively and have been observed in traffic; there are no unintended listening ports.
- The known NET-1 defect from #211 has been fixed and checked with appropriate regression testing; the existing canary does not count as a repair.

Builds on the accepted N01 foundation and B01. Native networking, native TLS and host prototypes retain separate evidence boundaries.
Existing work: #215; #39 only for network work that actually remains.
Source: [Security and PQC contract](https://github.com/simonvanieperen/nieuw-os/blob/6e429de98b5c692ccceaa12973818eecb1622062/docs/implementation/VERIFIABLE-SECURITY-AND-PQC.md).

Goal: protect personal content and sensitive metadata natively and enable independent recovery.

Complete when:
- Authenticated storage works after a cold restart; tampering, replay/rollback within the threat model and key loss produce controlled behaviour.
- Key management and recovery authorisation preserve domain and user boundaries.
- A user can create, verify and restore an independent backup and export data in documented formats.
- Interruption, full storage, loss and conflicts have been tested without silent overwriting.

Depends on B01 and S01–S08. B02 is required for reliable profile/session boundaries, E2E-NAS and external ciphertext storage.
